correctness.rationale: In characteristic at least five the degree-one anti-bicanonical double cover has the smooth canonical branch sextic used here. The Bertini pairing on the 240 exceptional curves is Galois-equivariant; the four degree types give one singleton family, two unordered-pair families and one triple family (use complements for the conics). In the cubic family Bertini exchanges the doubled and omitted point labels, so no ordering remains. An odd theta characteristic on this smooth genus-four curve has a unique effective divisor since h0 is odd and at most two by Clifford. The 120 labels thus count planes defined over the extension, not individually rational contacts. Independently generated all partitions of eight and evaluated the coefficients of the fixed-subset polynomial ∏(1+z^d) over the cycles of each power, truncating after z^3. The prefix counts are 13,20,22. The two-count collisions are (1,7)/(3,5) with third values 1/10 and (1,1,6)/(2,3,3) with third values 16/64. Divisor recursion from these fixed-subset formulas verifies every orbit spectrum in the frozen CSV and the finite étale zeta interpretation. For the field-size bound the three determinant families give 56·3+28·12+8·28=728 as a valid upper degree bound. The omitted cubic derivative is redundant by the affine chart and Euler's identity. Each determinant is nonzero on some tuple over the algebraic closure: evaluation functionals span the dual of the relevant polynomial space (for cubics, after imposing the value and two first derivatives at the chosen point, evaluate the resulting seven-dimensional subspace at seven suitably chosen points). The product is consequently nonzero. Squaring removes the relabeling sign. The linear Weil-restriction twist preserves nonvanishing and the degree bound; for q>1456 a nonzero polynomial of degree <q cannot vanish on the entire rational affine space. This gives distinct, general-position points of exactly the prescribed orbit type; duplicate points already make a triple determinant vanish.
residual_risks: The finite calculation checks the S8 action once the geometric correspondence is established. The proof gives a sufficient, not optimal, q-bound; the finite étale zeta function is not the curve or surface zeta function. The claim is about the first consecutive extension counts, not arbitrary pairs of extension degrees.

evidence: The partitions (1,7) and (3,5) have Carter symbols A6 and A4×A2 by Lemma 2.20; their types are 40 and 37 in Karras Table IV. Karras also uses exceptional-curve and surface point counts over extensions to tell Weyl types apart, not solely these three tritangent-plane counts. Trip's exact field-size statements concern specified Weyl types.
broader_coverage.reasoning: Karras gives genuinely stronger coverage of the realization of the two witnesses, not merely an isolated example. The determinant descent gives a short alternate sufficient bound, but the existence statement itself is covered. Weyl class recovery with different point/curve observables does not imply recovery from this shorter list of plane counts.

evidence: The explicit geometric labeling already reduces each individual count to fixed subsets of an eight-point permutation. In the Weyl table approach, if b is Bertini and w is Frobenius then T_n=(Fix_curves(w^n)+Fix_curves(bw^n))/2: a fixed pair has either two individually fixed members or two members swapped by w^n. Thus row and power data can be used to compute the profiles, and some claims, including the witness triples and their existence, are immediate from the prior table and realization theorem.
claim_vs_prior_implication.reasoning: Neither the existence of a full Weyl-class table nor recovery using other arithmetic observables entails a three-term separation theorem just by restricting the family. One must still compare the projected triples, since distinct spectra may have the same initial counts (indeed the two-count map collides). The credit here is for the exact short-prefix discrimination, not for rediscovering the curve spectra, fixed-subset labels, or sufficient realization fields.

originality.rationale: The distinct supported contribution is the uniform first-three tritangent-count discrimination on this S8 subfamily and its sharp prefix length. The geometric labeling, the possibility of obtaining profiles from existing exceptional-curve tables, and the existence of geometric witnesses are not separate originality claims. In particular Karras's prior work gives stronger realization coverage than q>1456, and its rows already supply the lower-bound collision after accounting for the Bertini pairs. Neither that table's classification of the Weyl types nor the different-observable inverse results inspected give the sufficiency of this particular short tritangent prefix: the comparison of those three projected counts across all 22 types is the key remaining result.
residual_risks: A prior projection of the Weyl-character data explicitly comparing these short tritangent signatures could overlap. The thesis full text was unavailable. The realization bound and individual computations from known tables are not assessed as original.

value.rationale: The meaningful finite cutoff is the minimum length of the initial count vector for a canonical finite étale scheme needed to recover the blow-up splitting class, without curve equations, contact-point rationality, full exceptional-curve spectra, or the full zeta function as input. Both the uniform three-count separation and the actual failure at two matter; merely reproducing existing exceptional-curve counts, or giving the weaker realization bound by itself, would not supply this value.
residual_risks: Only the marked S8 family and a particular prefix of extension degrees are covered, not all W(E8) forms or recovery of the full surface or curve data.
